newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold easier in Europe, mood remains bearish.
newsitem.headline: Gold easier in Europe, mood remains bearish.

text.p: Gold hovered below $340 an ounce in early Europe trading as speculation the IMF could sell some of its gold reserves to finance debt relief for poor countries cast a shadow over the market, dealers said.
Gold's move below $340 yesterday also undermined sentiment and had some traders thinking prices could test new lows.
"If we do not get back over $340 pretty soon, I think we are going to the year's low at $336. We will test that and see if we go any lower," one analyst at a major Swiss bank said.
Gold opened $339.00/$339.50, down from $339.80/$340.30 at the London close on Monday.

"Basically the mood is still negative," he added. "We keep hearing voices calling for IMF gold sales, and this shows that the whole environment of central bank selling is still playing a role in the market."
Silver was also lower, down three cents to $4.62/$4.64 after breaking support at $4.70 and touching two-year lows yesterday. Deaslers were eyeing a major chart point at $4.60.

Other metals were easier as well, following the recent pattern of price drops after the expiry of over-the-counter options. Platinum was off one dollar to $372.00/$373.00, while palladium slipped 75 cents to $156.00/$157.00.
"I think we are at the lower end of the range, but the market can turn on any news out of Russia," one dealer said.
